title: Dealer Gamma Exposure and Overnight Gap Risk: Incremental Information in Low-Volatility Regimes

detail.title: Dealer Gamma Exposure and Overnight Gap Risk: Incremental Information in Low-Volatility Regimes
detail.abstract: Dealer gamma exposure in S&P 500 options is widely claimed to predict realised volatility, with effects concentrated in stressed environments. I test that claim out of sample and find the opposite: against a properly specified Corsi HAR baseline with a corporate credit control, dealer gamma carries forecasting information about overnight gap magnitude only in low-VIX regimes. On stressed days the baseline already absorbs the signal; on calm days it is actively miscalibrated, and dealer gamma restores forecasting power. Pooling the two regimes washes out the effect, which is why prior work that did not split by regime may have missed it. Two orthogonal volatility predictors (VIX3M/VIX and CBOE SKEW) carry weaker calm-regime signals of their own, but a joint specification analysis locates the surviving forecasting power in the dealer-gamma-by-calm-regime interaction term. The result is robust to stress threshold, training cutoff, tenor, sign convention, and a Holm correction across one hundred Clark and West tests. At the deep upper tail used in Basel FRTB Expected Shortfall calculations (τ = 0.99), the augmented model reduces calm-regime quantile loss by roughly fifteen percent and stress-regime quantile loss by roughly six percent, with the largest forecasting payoff at the deep upper tail in both regimes. The economic implication is the inverse of the practitioner narrative: dealer gamma is most useful precisely where conventional volatility indicators are weakest.

title: A Regime-Filtered Intraday Trading Framework for Gold: Integrating VWAP Microstructure and EMA-Based Dynamic Exit Mechanisms

detail.title: A Regime-Filtered Intraday Trading Framework for Gold: Integrating VWAP Microstructure and EMA-Based Dynamic Exit Mechanisms
detail.abstract: This paper presents, formalises, and empirically validates a fully rule-based intraday trading strategy for gold spot (XAU/USD) that integrates Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) as a primary structural reference level with Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) as dynamic trend filters and trailing stop mechanisms. The strategy directly addresses two chronic structural inefficiencies in short-term gold trading: (i) the propensity of gold prices to produce aggressive intrabar wicks that prematurely trigger conventional fixeddistance stop-loss orders, and (ii) the difficulty of managing open profit as price approaches known institutional reference levels. The 200-period EMA serves as a binary regime classifier; entry is conditioned on a precisely defined pullback and rejection signal at the 50-period EMA above (or below) the session VWAP; and the 50-period EMA functions as a dynamic trailing stop activated exclusively on candle closes, not intrabar wick penetrations. All entry conditions are stated as machine-testable quantitative rules, eliminating hidden discretion. A simulated backtest over 247 trades on the XAU/USD 15-minute timeframe (January-December 2024) produces a win rate of 45.3%, mean expectancy of +0.414R per trade, profit factor of 1.76, annualised Sharpe ratio of 3.99, and maximum drawdown of 5.1% on a fixed 1% risk-per-trade model, substantially outperforming a simple EMA crossover benchmark across all evaluated metrics. Risk management incorporates ATR-adjusted position sizing, a hard daily loss limit, and explicit news-event exclusion protocols.

title: Does Crop Production Improve Farmer's Standard of Living? Mediation and Moderation Evidence from Meherpur, Bangladesh

detail.title: Does Crop Production Improve Farmer's Standard of Living? Mediation and Moderation Evidence from Meherpur, Bangladesh
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether higher crop production improves farmers' standard of living in Meherpur District, Bangladesh, and whether farm income mediates this relationship. Using cross-sectional survey data from 381 smallholder farmers, we employ an integrated empirical strategy: ordered logit and OLS with HC3-robust standard errors for the income equation; bootstrapped mediation analysis (5,000 replications, bias-corrected accelerated confidence intervals) for indirect-effect estimation; seemingly unrelated regression (SUR) for joint estimation of six welfare equations; principal component analysis (PCA) to assess welfare dimensionality; and interaction moderation to test whether farm size conditions the yield-welfare association. Three findings emerge. First, crop yield is positively associated with farm income (β̂ = 0.162, z = 31.1, p < 0.001; McFadden R² = 0.237), but years of farming experience carries a large negative coefficient (β̂ =-0.223, p < 0.001), suggesting that long-tenured smallholders face structural income disadvantages that experience alone cannot offset. Second, bootstrapped mediation indicates that farm income does not mediate the production-welfare relationship: all six indirect-effect 95% BCa confidence intervals include zero. OLS-HC3 estimates for each welfare outcome-monthly expenditure, healthcare visits, children's education, housing quality, rooms in the house, and healthcare facility rating-are uniformly small and statistically insignificant. Third, PCA reveals that the six welfare indicators are empirically orthogonal (Cronbach α =-0.010; PC1 accounts for 18.9% of variance), indicating that welfare in this setting is irreducibly multi-dimensional and that composite index construction is not statistically warranted. A significant Farm Size × Crop Yield interaction on housing quality (B =-0.129, p = 0.008) further suggests that yield gains benefit smaller farms modestly while leaving larger-farm households unaffected. Expenditure pressure-62.2% of farmers report monthly outgoings at or above farming income-provides a plausible mechanism through which income increments fail to reach welfare outcomes. Taken together, the evidence indicates that higher crop production raises farm income but does not translate into measurable improvements in household welfare under prevailing structural conditions in Meherpur. Yield-oriented programmes are necessary but insufficient for rural living-standard improvement; complementary investments in debt relief, market infrastructure, and social services are required.

title: Identifying Supply Effects of Universal Childcare Subsidies A Methodological Case Study from BC's $10-a-Day Program, with Descriptive Evidence on Provider Sorting

detail.title: Identifying Supply Effects of Universal Childcare Subsidies A Methodological Case Study from BC's $10-a-Day Program, with Descriptive Evidence on Provider Sorting
detail.abstract: British Columbia's $10-a-Day ChildCareBC program, launched in 2018 as Canada's first large-scale universal low-cost childcare initiative, offers a rare opportunity to study supply-side effects of universal childcare subsidies and to test the staggered difference-indifferences toolkit on a major Canadian provincial policy. Using a novel school-district-level panel (2018-2025) constructed from monthly administrative data, we apply a sequence of identification strategies and assess each through formal sensitivity analysis. The paper makes three contributions. First, on identification: a baseline event study with controls (Specification C) yields a positive and conventionally significant association at three to four years posttreatment, but Honest DiD sensitivity analysis (Rambachan and Roth 2023) shows this association does not survive post-period parallel-trends violations as small as half the worst pre-period violation (breakdown M ̄ < 0.5). Adding school-district-specific linear trends reverses the sign through a textbook manifestation of the Wolfers Paradox; the Callaway-Sant'Anna estimator yields a precise null driven by a fundamental composition shift that drops 27 of 59 districts. We document these failures explicitly as guidance for the broader Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care (CWELCC) evaluation literature. Second, on heterogeneity: we document a robust empirical pattern in which districts with lower preexisting coverage ("dry zones") exhibit substantially larger post-treatment supply expansion than wellserved districts. This descriptive heterogeneity gradient is itself sensitive to parallel-trends violations under formal testing, but the magnitude and timing pattern (growing from k = 0 to k = +4) is suggestive of a real two-phase mechanism that future work with longer pre-period data may be able to identify. Third, on provider sorting: we document 20 provider exits between announcement and the February 2026 active snapshot, concentrated among sole proprietors and small operators, with three distinguishable pathways-operator retirement, strategic reversion to market rates, and apparent facility closure. This descriptive evidence stands independently of the identification challenges above and provides a previously undocumented dimension of the universal-subsidy policy debate. We do not provide a credible causal point estimate of $10aDay's supply effect at this time. We discuss what data and design improvements would be required to do so, and what the present analysis nonetheless contributes to the ongoing CWELCC rollout.

title: Anticipatory Control and Reinforcement Learning: A Unified Theory

detail.title: Anticipatory Control and Reinforcement Learning: A Unified Theory
detail.abstract: This paper argues that anticipation is a mathematically clean axis along which classical control and reinforcement learning extend. The manuscript has two layers. First, it gives a unified synthesis of control, preview control, and reinforcement learning as the optimisation of a functional over an information-constrained policy class under dynamical evolution. Second, it concentrates theorem-level contributions in anticipatory control and anticipatory reinforcement learning. On the control side, the paper develops state-augmented LQR and LQG with an anticipatory Riccati equation, proves a preview separation principle via block decoupling of the augmented Kalman filter, formulates stochastic anticipatory control through filtration enlargement and value-of-information decompositions, and studies preview-aware operator-theoretic synthesis, Smith prediction, MPC, and H∞ design. The central quantitative result proves monotone benefit in the preview depth N together with a geometric diminishing-returns law governed by an effective preview radius ρeff; a scalar example verifies the generic ρ2 rate. On the learning side, the paper formulates the N-anticipatory MDP as the RL analogue of preview LQR, proves monotone preview benefit in MDPs, and gives an informal preview regret bound of order ˜O(√T poly(n,m)f(N)) for unknown linear systems. The theorem-level contribution is concentrated in Part V and in Section 33 of Part VI.

title: Nonsmooth Dynamics of Strategic Blockades: Energy Constraints and External Fragility in Small Open Economies

detail.title: Nonsmooth Dynamics of Strategic Blockades: Energy Constraints and External Fragility in Small Open Economies

detail.abstract: This paper develops a nonsmooth dynamic framework to analyze how strategic blockades transmit macroeconomic instability to small open economies (SOEs). It introduces the concept of an Energy-Remittance Double Shock (ERDS), in which external disruptions simultaneously constrain critical energy imports and reduce diaspora income inflows. The model is formulated as an optimal control problem with state and mixed constraints, where a physical limit on energy and a balance-of-payments constraint become endogenously binding. This generates regime shifts characterized by discontinuous shadow prices, non-differentiable value functions, and the breakdown of standard smoothing mechanisms. Within a Leontief production structure, binding energy constraints eliminate the marginal productivity of capital, leading to investment collapse and capital obsolescence. The analysis further shows that prolonged external disruptions can violate the transversality condition, and imply unsustainable debt dynamics and the impossibility of returning to the pre-shock growth path. Numerical solutions using a forward-backward sweep algorithm illustrate the model's dynamics for Bangladesh, while the framework can also be generalized to other developing economies exposed to strategic supply disruptions.

title: Beyond Labor Income: College Education and Housing Wealth Accumulation
affiliations: National University of Singapore, Peking University, Zhejiang University and

detail.title: Beyond Labor Income: College Education and Housing Wealth Accumulation
detail.abstract: We examine how education shapes financial decision-making through its effects on housing investment and leverage. Exploiting China’s unexpected 1999 college-enrollment expansion, which increased admissions by nearly 50 percent in a single year, we implement a regression-discontinuity design around the relevant county-specific cohort cutoff. Households whose heads were more likely to attend college are 6.0 percentage points more likely to own commercial housing and allocate a share of income to housing that is 13 percent higher than that of the untreated cohort. Underlying this pattern is the more active usage of mortgage credit among the treated cohort: they are 4.4 percentage points more likely to have a mortgage, with loan-to-value higher by 23 percent. Although both groups earn largely similar rates of housing return, the treated cohort’s larger exposure to housing assets leads to substantially higher housing-wealth appreciation, with an annualized gain of RMB 17,000, about 105 percent higher than that of untreated cohorts. This housing-wealth appreciation gap is roughly three times as large as the labor-income premium from college expansion. Further analysis suggests these housing responses are primarily driven by investment motives and are unexplained by cohort effects. A calibrated life-cycle model shows that ignoring housing understates the welfare return to college by more than half.

title: Can Anti-corruption Policy Grease the Wheels of Growth? A Quasi-natural Experiment
affiliations: Beijing Wuzi University,  and Beijing Wuzi University

detail.title: Can Anti-corruption Policy Grease the Wheels of Growth? A Quasi-natural Experiment
detail.abstract: In this study, we investigate the causal links between anti-corruption and economic growth by designing a framework of quasi-natural experiment between the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China and Mongolia. Our analysis advances the existing literature in three ways. First, to our knowledge, this is the first quasi-natural experiment from a macroeconomic perspective that examines the effects of the anti-corruption policy on economic growth. Second, the impacts of corruption on economic performance have been largely explored, but little is known in the extensive existing literature about the effects of anti-corruption on economic growth. Finally, the results of Bacon decomposition suggest that the anti-corruption policy is beneficial to growth, which approximately increases the annual growth rate of per capita GDP by 1.6 percentage points. Our results survive a battery of heterogeneity and robustness tests.

title: Retail Prices of Gasoline and Asymmetric Adjustment to Wholesale Prices in Colombia

detail.title: Retail Prices of Gasoline and Asymmetric Adjustment to Wholesale Prices in Colombia

keywords: Gasoline Retail Markets JEL Classification: Q40

detail.abstract: This study examines the pass-through between retail and wholesale prices of gasoline in Colombia. Data from 2017 to 2019 were available on prices and characteristics of gasoline sold by service stations in the main cities of Colombia. Information on the location of the stations is also available, which is used to georeference the stations and obtain the potential number of competitors for a station. The study results show an asymmetric pass-through behavior between retail and wholesale prices. Furthermore, the potential number of competitors of the stations has a direct effect on the retail prices and an indirect effect because it alters the stations' pass-through.

title: Has the regulatory cycle weakened? Evidence from a century of financial legislation *
affiliations: Humboldt University of Berlin, Department of History and Humboldt University of Berlin

detail.title: Has the regulatory cycle weakened? Evidence from a century of financial legislation *
detail.abstract: The regulatory cycle view suggests that periods of deregulation encourage increased risk-taking, which in turn leads to financial crises and subsequent re-regulation. To test this proposition, we develop a novel 10-item index capturing prudential and structural banking regulation across 14 countries over the past century. We find that deregulation is indeed associated with heightened risk appetite and credit expansion. However, the regulatory response to financial crises has changed significantly over time. Consistent with the financial trilemma, the evidence suggests that the cycle has weakened, as open capital accounts are increasingly incompatible with effective regulation at the national level.

title: Effect of Social Information on Competition Choice
affiliations: Indian Institute of Management Bangalore, Monash University, Azim Premji University and Indian Institute of Management (IIMB), Bangalore - Department of Economics and Social Sciences

detail.title: Effect of Social Information on Competition Choice

keywords: Willingness to Compete JEL Code: C90 D83 D90

detail.abstract: We examine how social information about competition choices influences individuals' willingness to compete. Participants perform a real-effort task under both piece-rate and tournament incentives, and subsequently make competition choices in two rounds. Between rounds, we exogenously vary the information provided about others' choices across three treatments. We find that social information about the proportion of participants who chose to compete in the first round significantly affects the willingness to compete in the second round. This effect is not driven by the salience of the incentive schemes. Observing a lower rate of competition among peers increases an individual's propensity to enter the tournament. This evidence is consistent with predictions from a rational model of Bayesian learning, in which individuals strategically choose to compete based on their treatment-induced belief about the average ability of other participants.

title: Exchange Rate Shocks to Working Capital, Financing Frictions and Real Fragility
affiliations: Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, Bilkent University - Faculty of Business Administration and Government of the Republic of Turkey - Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey

detail.title: Exchange Rate Shocks to Working Capital, Financing Frictions and Real Fragility
detail.abstract: We examine how exchange rate shocks propagate to firm outcomes and amplify through working capital and financing frictions. Guided by a model with cash-in-advance constraints on production and external borrowing constraints based on pledgeable income, our analysis exploits firm-specific seasonality and foreign exchange surprises for empirical identification. Using an extensive array of administrative datasets from Türkiye (2010-2024), we find that currency depreciations arriving in main quarters trigger significantly larger contractions in purchases, sales, and production than depreciations in non-main quarters. Bank credit also tightens, with sharper reductions in short-term loans than long-term loans. These effects are strongest for SMEs, highly leveraged, and import-dependent firms, while large firms expand borrowing in line with a flight-to-quality. Construction and services with long cash conversion cycles are particularly exposed. Our results establish a novel source of fragility in production due to working capital and financing frictions: depreciation-induced increases in input costs force cuts in purchases, reduce sales and pledgeable income, and tighten short-term external finance, deepening real economic contractions.

title: The supply of human enhancement technologies

detail.title: The supply of human enhancement technologies
detail.abstract: We study the supply-side direction of innovation in human enhancement technologies whose effects are inheritable across generations or confined to the treated individual. In a three-generation framework with heterogeneous agents, binding budget constraints, uncertainty about outcomes, and the possibility of imitation by entrants, inheritability creates a distinctive appropriability problem: a single purchase generates benefits for future descendants, but firms cannot charge those future beneficiaries. This intergenerational non-appropriability can reverse the private ranking of projects relative to their social value, leading decentralized research to favor non-inheritable enhancements even when inheritable ones maximize welfare, under high risk and limited entry to tilt excessively toward inheritability. We characterize equilibrium timing, the conditions under which innovation is inefficiently directed, and how inequality shapes adoption and profits. We also extend the model to competing researchers and show that standard congestion effects do not eliminate the core wedge between private incentives and social efficiency.

title: Why qualifications matter in the early years workforce.

detail.title: Why qualifications matter in the early years workforce.
detail.abstract:
It is well established that skilled, well-qualified practitioners are widely recognised as essential to high- quality early education and care (Nutbrown, 2021; Pascal, Bertram and Cole-Albäck, 2020; Bull et al, 2024). Yet in the UK, concerns persist about the disconnect between the demands of early years practice alongside the policy rhetoric of the importance of early years education for children’s learning and development, and the qualifications and professional status assigned to practitioners (Bonetti, 2018; Pascal, Bertram and Cole- Albäck, 2020; Nutbrown, 2021).

Against this backdrop of persistent challenges, Early Education’s (2025) study provides a timely, in-depth examination of how qualifications serve as a cornerstone of workforce professionalisation across the four UK nations. Drawing on the data, this article explores how qualification requirements shape entry into the profession, career progression, and graduate leadership. By focusing on qualifications, the study highlights both barriers and opportunities within current systems and considers what a coherent qualification structure might look like to support a skilled, sustainable early years workforce across the UK.

O presente artigo analisa os Avisos nºs 09 e 10/2024, de 20 de dezembro, do Banco Nacional
de Angola (BNA), avaliando o seu desenho normativo e os potenciais impactos sobre o
financiamento à habitação, à construção e aos sectores produtivos prioritários da economia
angolana. Num contexto de elevada incidência de crédito malparado (cujo rácio ultrapassou 20%
nos últimos anos) e de crónica insuficiência de financiamento bancário a sectores não
petrolíferos, o estudo problematiza a tensão entre estabilidade financeira e expansão do crédito
à economia real. A metodologia é qualitativa, assente em análise documental dos diplomas
normativos, revisão da literatura especializada em intermediação financeira, risco de crédito e
regulação bancária, e confronto com boas práticas internacionais. A análise demonstra que os
Avisos introduzem inovações regulatórias relevantes: taxas de juro máximas favorecidas (7%
para crédito habitacional e 7,5% para investimento produtivo), mecanismos de dedução das
reservas obrigatórias, requisitos mínimos de operações com mecanismo comply or explain e
critérios detalhados de elegibilidade e avaliação de risco. Identificam-se, porém, desafios de
implementação: sustentabilidade financeira das operações para os bancos, limitada capacidade
técnica de avaliação sectorial, eficácia dos mecanismos de garantia e execução judicial, e
viabilidade efectiva dos projectos a financiar. Conclui-se que os Avisos constituem uma iniciativa
regulatória coerente e tecnicamente fundamentada, cujos resultados dependerão da capacidade
institucional das instituições financeiras, da evolução macroeconómica e da articulação com
políticas complementares de apoio aos sectores visados.

title: Opening History's Shareholder Activism Black Box
affiliations: University of Cambridge - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Opening History's Shareholder Activism Black Box
detail.abstract: Shareholder activism is a pivotal element of corporate governance. Historical analysis of shareholder engagement in publicly traded companies has nevertheless generally been cursory. This paper draws upon a hand-collected dataset of proxy contests compiled from newspaper archives to correct matters for the United States for the first half of the 20 th century. The dataset reveals shareholder engagement occurred with greater frequency than conventional wisdom implies, particularly in the 1930s and the 1940s. Moreover, the stakes were typically high, with corporate control often being in play by way of contests for directorships. The paper accounts for the trends the proxy contest dataset reveals by reference to applicable corporate law rules and incentives shareholders potentially had to launch proxy contests.

title: The Molecule Economy: A Paradigm Shift from Crude Oil as Fuel to 'Mother Matter' via Project-Based RWA Tokenization

detail.title: The Molecule Economy: A Paradigm Shift from Crude Oil as Fuel to 'Mother Matter' via Project-Based RWA Tokenization
detail.abstract: In the 21st century, the utilization of crude oil as a primary energy source (combustion) is not only environmentally challenging but also represents a major economic inefficiency in the value chain. This paper introduces a new model entitled "The Molecule Economy," where crude oil is redefined as "Mother Matter" for high-tech manufacturing rather than a burnable commodity. The transition requires significant downstream investment; thus, this research proposes an innovative methodology based on Real World Asset (RWA) Tokenization for project-based financing. By issuing tokens backed by in-situ reserves and future project cash flows, liquidity for advanced petrochemical units is secured. Strategic analysis indicates that this approach can increase the value-added per barrel by up to 300% compared to the raw export model, mitigating risks associated with the global energy transition.

title: **Constraint-Bound Exposure Instruments (CBEI): A Formal Specification of a New Financial Instrument Class**

detail.title: **Constraint-Bound Exposure Instruments (CBEI): A Formal Specification of a New Financial Instrument Class**
detail.abstract: This paper defines Constraint-Bound Exposure Instruments (CBEIs) as a distinct class of financial instruments that provide exposure to outcomes resolved within a constrained system, without conferring ownership, control, or enforceable claim on underlying assets, outputs, or cash flows. Unlike equity, debt, or derivatives, CBEIs do not encode entitlement or payoff functions. Instead, they encode non-entitled exposure to system-resolved states under externally sovereign constraints. We formalise the structure, boundary conditions, and invariants of CBEIs, demonstrate their non-equivalence to derivatives, and introduce a registry specification (CBEI-RS v1.0) for validation and classification. A reference implementation is provided through Alignment Bonds within the u-Kama ecological coordination system. CBEIs establish a financial primitive suitable for domains where truth must remain independent of financial influence. Alignment Bonds may be transferred or traded in external markets without restriction by the issuing system. They remain associated with the ecological cells to which they were originally linked and are externally legible to BIO outcomes arising from those cells, where such outcomes are independently issued under protocol conditions. This association confers no entitlement, claim, conversion right, priority, or guarantee of BIO allocation, and no external market activity may influence ecological verification, qualification, or issuance. Alignment Bonds are non-redeemable by the issuing system and may be transferred or sold to third parties in external markets. Any market price or valuation is determined entirely outside the system and exerts no influence on ecological verification, qualification, or BIO issuance.

title: Governing Autonomous Intelligence: Risks, Accountability, and Control in the Era of Agentic AI

detail.title: Governing Autonomous Intelligence: Risks, Accountability, and Control in the Era of Agentic AI
detail.abstract: The emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI)-systems capable of autonomous decision-making and goal-directed behavior-marks a significant evolution in the trajectory of digital technologies. Unlike traditional AI models, agentic systems operate with increased independence, adaptability, and capacity to act in complex environments, raising profound governance challenges. This article examines the risks associated with agentic AI, including loss of human oversight, accountability gaps, systemic vulnerabilities, and ethical concerns. It explores existing and emerging regulatory approaches, with particular attention to the European Union's evolving framework for AI governance. The paper argues that effective governance of autonomous intelligence requires a multi-layered approach that integrates legal, technical, and institutional mechanisms. It concludes by proposing policy recommendations aimed at ensuring accountability, maintaining human control, and fostering trust in increasingly autonomous digital systems.

title: Strategy Rescaling and the Stability of Kantian Optimization

detail.title: Strategy Rescaling and the Stability of Kantian Optimization

detail.abstract: This study investigates the properties and stability of the Multiplicative Kantian Equilibrium (MKE) in symmetric games. We first demonstrate that MKE lacks strategic equivalence: the Kantian best-response function is not invariant under monotonic strategy rescaling. This strategic non-equivalence implies that the choice of measurement scalea subjective interpretation of the gamematerially impacts equilibrium outcomes. Exploiting this nonequivalence, in a game where players may be Kantian or Nasher, we propose an efficient strategy rescaling that allows Kantians to neutralize the free-rider advantage of Nashers, while preserving Pareto-efficient outcomes among themselves. In a dynamic framework, we show that the subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium with endogenous choice of optimization type leads all players to prefer Kantian optimization over Nash optimization. In an evolutionary setup, we show that Kantian optimization is an evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS). Our results suggest that the inherent strategic non-equivalence of Kantian optimization provides a robust pathway to stable cooperation.

title: ERP-Enabled ESG Reporting and Financial Transparency Under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 Transformation Framework

detail.abstract: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting is increasingly recognized as a critical component of financial transparency frameworks supporting sustainable economic diversification across emerging markets. Within Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 transformation strategy, infrastructure-sector organizations face growing expectations to strengthen sustainability disclosure practices aligned with international reporting standards. This study examines how Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems such as SAP ERP and Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP support ESG reporting readiness through centralized data integration, procurement governance transparency, asset lifecycle monitoring, and compliance-aligned reporting architectures. Using a qualitative policy-oriented analytical framework, the study evaluates how digitally integrated accounting information systems improve disclosure reliability and institutional transparency across infrastructure-sector reporting environments undergoing regulatory modernization. The findings suggest that ERP-enabled ESG reporting environments represent a foundational component of sustainability disclosure architectures supporting investor confidence, governance accountability, and participation in sustainability-oriented capital-market environments aligned with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 transformation objectives.

title: Antibiotic Resistance: Mechanisms, Epidemiology, and Contemporary Therapeutic Strategies — a Comprehensive Review

detail.title: Antibiotic Resistance: Mechanisms, Epidemiology, and Contemporary Therapeutic Strategies — a Comprehensive Review

detail.abstract: Antibiotic resistance (ABR) is one of the most critical public health emergencies of the twentyfirst century, threatening to erode the therapeutic gains achieved over decades of antimicrobial innovation. According to the WHO Global Antibiotic Resistance Surveillance Report 2025, approximately one in six laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections worldwide in 2023 were resistant to antibiotic treatment, with resistance increasing in over 40% of monitored pathogendrug combinations between 2018 and 2023. The Global Research on Antimicrobial Resistance (2024) further estimated that 4.71 million deaths were associated with bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2021 alone. This review synthesises current evidence on the classification of antibiotics, the molecular and genetic mechanisms driving resistance, the ecology of soil-derived antibiotic producers, and the clinical epidemiology of major drug-resistant pathogens. It further discusses the evolving landscape of novel antimicrobial agentsincluding recently approved drugs such as ceftobiprole, gepotidacin, sulopenem etzadroxil, and pivmecillinamalongside contemporary strategies including antibiotic stewardship, One Health surveillance frameworks, and subscription-based economic models for antibiotic development. Special attention is paid to the African and Nigerian context, where the burden of resistant organisms such as MRSA, MDR-TB, and ESBL-producing Enterobacteriaceae remains substantial yet surveillance capacity continues to lag behind global standards. This review underscores the urgency of integrated, multisectoral responses to preserve the efficacy of antibiotics for future generations.

title: The Transmission of Monetary Policy under the Microscope a

detail.abstract: We investigate the transmission of monetary policy to household consumption using administrative data on the universe of households in Norway. Based on identified monetary policy shocks, we estimate the dynamic responses of consumption, income, and saving along the liquid asset distribution of households. For low-liquidity but also for high-liquidity households, changes in disposable income are associated with a sizable consumption reaction. The impact consumption response is closely linked to interest rate exposure, which is negative at the bottom but positive at the top of the distribution. Indirect effects of monetary policy gradually build up and eventually outweigh the direct effects.

title: Role of Model Selection in Weak Instrumental Variable Analysis
affiliations: , University of Cambridge - MRC Biostatistics Unit and University of Cambridge

detail.title: Role of Model Selection in Weak Instrumental Variable Analysis
detail.abstract: A common device used to evaluate the sufficiency of instrument strength is the F-Test, where we perform an IV analysis if and only if {F > k} is satisfied. We call this selecting on the F-Test; we analyse how it impacts the performance of estimators under weak instruments, by adopting the local-to-zero asymptotics studied in Staiger and Stock (1997) and Stock and Yogo (2005). Such a selection on the F-Test is an example of model selection bias, or equivalently, publication bias. We find conditioning on passing this F-Test reduces mean squared error of the 2SLS estimator when the amount of unmeasured confounding present is sufficiently small, while aggravating the mean squared error when unmeasured confounding is sufficiently big. We next investigate the effect selecting on an F-Test has on type I error rate of the Wald test. We find this inflates type I error rate of the Wald test and that this inflation is aggravated the more unmeasured confounding present. We provide intuition for these observations both graphically and by presenting this effect of model selection in terms of collider bias on a directed acyclic graph. Finally, we revise the critical values required for assessing the sufficiency of instrument strength, taking into account the impact of model selection bias. We find the required critical values for guaranteeing mean squared error are smaller when factoring in model selection bias. When model selection bias is taken into account, we find that performing no F-Test at all provides better guarantees on the type I error rate of the Wald Test than if one uses the conventionally used critical values in Stock and Yogo (2005) or the F > 10 rule of thumb.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the association between the real (affordability adjusted) cost of a recommended healthy diet and community-level child stunting in Nigeria, using nationally representative panel data. Nonparametric local polynomial estimates reveal a positive and nonlinear relationship: the share of stunted children rises sharply over a middle range of the cost distribution, with the gradient notably steeper in hotter and arid communities. Parametric (OLS) regressions with relevant community-level controls confirm the positive association. These findings suggest that local food affordability is an important predictor of child malnutrition.

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a theoretical framework to analyze housing price formation in markets with heterogeneous demand and fixed supply. Building on a marginal-buyer approach, the model endogenizes the composition of buyers through entry and selection mechanisms.

The key result is that the sensitivity of housing prices to local income is not structural, but depends on the probability that the marginal buyer is local. As external demand increases, the marginal buyer becomes more likely to be external, weakening the relationship between housing prices and local economic conditions.

The framework provides a microfoundation for observed variation in price–income elasticities across markets and over time. It also offers a conceptual basis for understanding housing affordability challenges in small open and globally exposed regions.

title: Takeoffs and Test Scores: The Impact of Noise Pollution on Standardized Test Performance

detail.title: Takeoffs and Test Scores: The Impact of Noise Pollution on Standardized Test Performance
detail.abstract: Noise pollution has become so ubiquitous in urban life that it is generally considered innocuous. However, research suggests that noise pollution can be more than a minor distraction and is associated with diminished health and productivity. I leverage exogenous shifts in noise pollution from a change in commercial flight paths and use a value-added model that accounts for student ability and school quality to estimate the causal impact of airplane noise pollution on standardized test performance. I find a large negative impact on math test performance, but no impact on English language art test performance. Moving from a school at the 25th percentile of exposure to one at the 75th percentile is associated with a math test score reduction of 0.05 standard deviations, larger than the impact of missing 10 school days during the year. Additionally, I find evidence that these negative impacts may be driven by the loudest days. These findings suggest a potentially large value to investing in noise insulation for schools exposed to high noise levels.

detail.abstract: This research aims to investigate the impact of AI based health recommendations and healthcare professionals on consumer decision making while purchasing over the counter (OTC) products in India. This study employs a quantitative descriptive survey conducted by means of a structured online questionnaire, to which 150 responses were gathered. Consumer awareness, usage, levels of trust and their purchase behavior with respect to both AI tools and professional recommendations are evaluated. The research reveals that, while a substantial number of consumers are aware and are using the AI based tools to retrieve information about health care related aspects, they have maximum faith in healthcare professionals over the former. A much greater percentage of respondents reported making OTC purchases following the suggestions of either a doctor or a pharmacist over AI based suggestions. The research concludes that, although the AI based platforms play a role in increasing consumer awareness and purchase ease; their contribution to final purchase decision is rather minimal and that a consumers decision making continues to remain mostly driven by the credibility of a healthcare professional.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how monetary policy jointly affects asset prices and the real economy in the United States. I develop an estimator that uses high-frequency surprises as a proxy for the structural monetary policy shocks. This is achieved by integrating the surprises into a vector autoregressive model as an exogenous variable. I use current short-term rate surprises because these are least affected by an information effect. When allowing for time-varying model parameters, I find that, compared to the response of output, the reaction of stock and house prices to monetary policy shocks was particularly low before the 2007-09 financial crisis.

detail.abstract:
This teaching note provides a step-by-step numerical illustration of a housing price formation model with heterogeneous demand and fixed supply. Building on a marginal-buyer framework, the note shows how equilibrium prices are determined by the composition of buyers at the margin.

Through a simple calibrated example, the note demonstrates how an increase in external demand raises equilibrium prices and increases the probability that the marginal buyer is external. As a result, the sensitivity of housing prices to local income declines.

The objective is pedagogical: to make the intuition of the model transparent and accessible, and to illustrate the link between marginal-buyer composition and price–income sensitivity.

title: Skills are Power: AI in a Labor Market with Asymmetric Skill Substitution
affiliations: Fudan University and University of International Business and Economics

detail.title: Skills are Power: AI in a Labor Market with Asymmetric Skill Substitution
detail.abstract: We develop a novel perspective on how AI impacts the labor market. Higher-skill workers may perform tasks that require only lower skills but not the other way around. This generates overskilling where the same task is performed by labor of different skill levels. Skills are the (only) source of market power. Competing in a larger segment of jobs, higher skills command higher wages while securing a greater distance from non-employment, which is then only relevant for people at the bottom of the skill spectrum. This skill-based story of market power also suggests that the allocation of any economic surplus brought by AI is skewed towards the top of the skill distribution. Specific predictions are made as to when AI reduces or raises non-employment, and under what conditions non-employment occurs broadly to produce mass non-employment. In particular, until AI replaces all the low-skill jobs or drives the wages in the jobs below the AI-replacement set down to their minimum levels, AI reduces rather than increases non-employment, as all displaced workers will find reemployment in a neighboring segment of the labor market where new jobs are created because of higher labor productivity. The model also suggests that sufficiently low AI costs are necessary for large scale non-employment.

detail.abstract:
Housing affordability has become a structural challenge in many supply-constrained and globally exposed housing markets. This paper argues that conventional policy approaches fail because they do not address the underlying mechanism of price formation.

Building on a marginal-buyer framework, the paper shows that housing prices are determined by the segment of demand with the highest willingness to pay. As external demand becomes more influential, prices decouple from local income, even when external buyers represent a minority of transactions.

The paper reframes the problem as a failure of institutional design rather than a standard market failure. It proposes the Insular Territorial Equilibrium Framework (MIET), an approach to land market design based on the functional differentiation of land into residential, intermediate, and patrimonial segments.

By separating demand segments with structurally different purchasing power, the framework modifies the conditions under which prices are formed, restoring the link between housing access and local economic conditions in the residential segment without direct price intervention.

title: Detecting Informed Trading Before Unscheduled Geopolitical Announcements: Evidence from Cross-Asset Futures Volume

detail.title: Detecting Informed Trading Before Unscheduled Geopolitical Announcements: Evidence from Cross-Asset Futures Volume
detail.abstract:
This paper develops and applies a cross-asset informed-flow detection framework to CME ES (S&P 500 E-mini) and CL (WTI crude oil) futures surrounding six unscheduled geopolitical announcements during the Iran conflict of March-April 2026. Using 1-minute OHLCV bars from Databento (GLBX.MDP3), the framework identifies bars where simultaneous volume anomalies in both instruments are directionally consistent with the content of the subsequent announcement. The framework detects cross-asset spikes that are statistically unlikely under a random-timing null preceding two de-escalation announcements: E004 (CL Z=11.93, return -31.5 bps, T-16 minutes) and E007 (ES Z=8.54, CL Z=14.01, return -244.7 bps on CL, T-167 minutes). Findings are robust across 320 parameter combinations (100% confirmation rate, 0% false positive rate on control events). A within-window Fisher combined test yields p=0.0035. The analysis demonstrates that publicly available 1-minute exchange data can detect cross-asset informed flow before unscheduled geopolitical announcements without access to position-level or order-flow data. All code is reproducible with a free Databento API key.
Replication code: https://github.com/ychly/informed-flow-detection

detail.title: XXV International Congress of Young Scientists “Traditions and Innovations in Modern Russian Law” Section “International Taxation in the Middle of 21 Century” Report “The Concept of “Technical Services” for Tax Purposes in International Transactions”
detail.abstract: The article analyses the concept of “technical services” for tax purposes in international transactions. It highlights the lack of a clear definition, which taxpayers exploit to avoid taxation in source countries—especially developing ones. In response, the 2021 UN Model Convention introduced Article 12A, allowing source countries to tax fees for technical services similarly to royalties. These services are defined as managerial, technical, or consulting activities requiring specialized knowledge or skills, excluding routine services, employment-related payments, and personal services. The OECD Model lacks similar provisions, leaving a gap. Bilateral tax treaties vary widely: for example, India’s treaties with Germany use broad definitions, while the US-India treaty includes a “make available clause” requiring transfer of technical knowledge. Russian treaties with India, Malaysia, and Botswana also contain broad definitions. The author concludes that while including technical services provisions promotes fair tax allocation, the absence of a universal definition leads to either overly broad interpretations or fragmented country-specific rules, potentially distorting service provider behaviour and undermining tax equity between developed and developing nations.

title: Start, Trajectory, Consistency: A Conceptual Framework for Student-Level Behavioral Engagement Profiling

detail.title: Start, Trajectory, Consistency: A Conceptual Framework for Student-Level Behavioral Engagement Profiling
detail.abstract: How is this individual student engaging right now-across all their courses simultaneouslyand what does that tell the institution about how to act? This question sits at the heart of student success practice: it is what advisors are trying to answer when they reach out, what IR offices are trying to surface when they build dashboards, and what student success programs are trying to detect before it is too late. Yet it remains unanswered by current institutional analytics. Learning analytics describes how students engage within individual learning environments-in higher education, most commonly courses. Student success research describes who students are demographically and contextually. Neither constructs the student-level behavioral picture that institutional action requires. This paper introduces the Start, Trajectory, Consistency (STC) Engagement Profile: a conceptual framework that constructs three behavioral dimensions from institutional data that already exists, aggregated to the student level across the full course load, and governed by four signal selection principles. STC enables two institutional implications-targeted intervention before outcomes deteriorate, and pattern learning across measurement periods to discover which engagement dimensions consistently connect to institutional outcomes. Of the three dimensions, Consistency is the most novel contribution, capturing how regularly and consistently a student performs their engagement behaviors-a property that no current institutional framework constructs or measures.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a forensic economic analysis of speculative dynamics in the Islamabad-Rawalpindi real estate corridor, with particular attention to the structural mechanics of the 'Greater Fool Theory' as it manifests in Pakistan's off-plan property sector. The analysis demonstrates that the market is sustained not by urbanization-driven end-user demand but by a self-reinforcing cycle of file trading, undocumented capital absorption, and developer incentive engineering. Drawing on regulatory data, market indices from the Global Property Guide, Pakistan Institute of Development Economics research, and documented case studies of developer failures, the paper calculates a Price-to-Income ratio of 90.8 for Islamabad as of early 2026, a figure approximately eighteen times the international affordability threshold. The paper further examines the structural failure of the Islamabad Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2020, the forensic irregularities embedded in guaranteed rental yield schemes, the legal status of over 117 unauthorized housing societies identified by the CDA, and the compounding effects of the 2025 global tariff environment on construction costs and buyer liquidity. The paper concludes that the market presents a HIGH risk profile for collapse, and that the 'last buyer' in file-trading chains faces a disproportionate probability of unrecoverable financial loss in the absence of immediate regulatory intervention.

detail.abstract: This article examines the socially equitable taxation of individual income and real estate in the People's Republic of China. Rooted in the 1949 principle of fair distribution of tax burden, China’s tax system relies primarily on direct taxes. The individual income tax features a high tax-exempt threshold (60,000 yuan annually) and a progressive rate structure (from 3% to 45%), effectively exempting most low- and middle-income earners while shifting the burden onto the wealthy. Additionally, China provides a national mechanism to eliminate international double taxation. Property tax is generally levied only on commercially used or rented real estate, avoiding double taxation of already-taxed income. Based on this analysis, the author suggests that Russia could adopt similar measures, including a non-taxable minimum income, mechanisms to prevent international double taxation, and a non-taxable portion of non-commercial real estate value. These reforms would increase disposable income for individuals, potentially boosting VAT revenues and offsetting losses from direct tax reductions.

detail.abstract: The financial services industry is at an inflection point. As transaction volumes scale exponentially and financial crime networks become increasingly sophisticated, traditional Anti-Money Laundering (AML) systems-built on deterministic, rule-based architectures-are no longer fit for purpose. detail.abstract:
This proposal outlines the United States All-American Apex (USAAA) Index Fund, a theoretical policy initiative designed to resolve the projected 2033 insolvency of the Social Security Trust Fund. By modernizing the Social Security Administration’s (SSA) 1935 investment mandate, the USAAA transitions the fund from an exclusive reliance on low-yield Treasury bonds to a diversified, high-performance equity engine.

The framework introduces a "50/50 Safety Split," maintaining a 50% statutory safety floor in U.S. Treasuries while allocating the remaining 50% into the "Apex 110"—a meritocratic selection of the top 10 corporate drivers across the 11 GICS sectors. Utilizing a sector-normalized weighting system, the model mitigates systemic risk while intending to capture equity returns of 7–10%.

Key strategic outcomes include:

  • Self-Sustaining Solvency: Closing the Social Security Solvency funding gap without increasing payroll taxes or reducing benefits.

  • National Economic Velocity: Incentivizing domestic corporate growth and R&D through inclusion in the national portfolio.

  • Institutional Governance: Establishing a non-partisan Federal Investment Board (FIB) to ensure automated, transparent oversight.

Through the "Apex" methodology, this initiative aligns the retirement security of American workers with the broader success of the U.S. economy, securing long-term fiscal resilience and national prosperity.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines monetary sustainability as the central functional precondition for state governance under uncertainty. The core argument: Monetary sovereignty is not a technical capability but a trust resource. Without trust in the currency's future purchasing power, the state loses its capacity to act—regardless of constitutional powers or central bank independence.

The analysis demonstrates that debt sustainability is not determined by debt-to-GDP ratios but by market confidence. When trust erodes, even low debt levels become unsustainable. Historical cases (Weimar hyperinflation, Argentine peso crises, 2010s Eurozone) illustrate how trust loss triggers self-fulfilling prophecies: Rising interest rates increase debt service, forcing either monetization (destroying trust further) or austerity (undermining political legitimacy).

The paper argues that monetary sustainability cannot be engineered through rules alone. It requires credible commitment to price stability and fiscal discipline—backed by institutions and actors willing to enforce painful decisions when markets doubt state solvency. Without this commitment capacity, even sound policies fail to restore trust once lost.

title: The Safe Asset Cliff: Demographic Downgrade Risk and Collateral Scarcity

detail.title: The Safe Asset Cliff: Demographic Downgrade Risk and Collateral Scarcity
detail.abstract: Population aging simultaneously increases demand for safe sovereign assets and undermines the fiscal foundations of safe issuers. This paper develops a probabilistic model of sovereign downgrade risk linked to demographic aging and traces the consequences of crossing the safe-issuer threshold through the regulatory architecture of global finance. Using a 31-country panel of S&P sovereign ratings (1990-2024), I estimate ordered logit and PanelGLS models that identify a critical OADR threshold: above 20% old-age dependency, each additional percentage point of aging reduces sovereign ratings by 9.6 points on the 21-point S&P scale (β =-21.8, p < 0.001 on the spline term). Monte Carlo simulations project that the number of safe issuers (AAor above) falls from 24 to a median of 13.5 by mid-century, with the safe supply ratio declining from 0.89 to 0.77. The consequences of crossing the cliff depend on financial structure: France, with over €3 trillion in sovereign debt and majority non-resident holdings, would trigger cross-border repricing through the Basel III risk-weight discontinuity (0% to 20%) while reactivating the eurozone sovereign-bank nexus; Japan, by contrast, has crossed the cliff quietly because domestic holding dominance and central bank absorption contain the adjustment. The prudential regime is politically entrenched: the Basel Committee's 2017 reform discussion produced no action, and the March 2026 US Basel III Endgame reproposal retained the 0% sovereign risk weight. The regulatory architecture guarantees that the demographic downgrade, when it arrives, will produce abrupt repricing rather than gradual adjustment.

detail.abstract: This paper extends the Bitcoin Media Pressure Index (BMPI) developed in Parfenovich (2026, SSRN Working Paper No. 6542901)-a daily media-sentiment signal derived from GDELT Global Knowledge Graph 2.0-from a validated signal into a systematic portfolio construction tool. Using 3,800 daily observations spanning September 2015 through January 2026, we demonstrate that BMPI, which measures the information environment around Bitcoin through normalised mention volume and coverage tone, can govern dynamic exposure in a way that improves risk-adjusted performance. A cascade allocation strategy (V9, SHARPE_MODE) that scales position size according to BMPI-defined regimes-supplemented by volatility targeting and drawdown protection-achieves an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio of 2.27 and a maximum drawdown of-16.6% on a 1,120-day test window (December 2022-January 2026), versus 1.38 and-32.6% for passive buy-and-hold. We do not claim that BMPI forecasts return direction; the mechanism is exposure management, not market timing. The Jensen alpha is +0.418 per annum (t = 3.864, p < 0.001, HAC-corrected). A permutation test comparing BMPI-weighted against fixed-weight allocation yields p = 0.029. In a live-deployment scenario with expanding-window BMPI calibration, the strategy retains its performance characteristics. BMPI-based allocation survives doubled transaction costs and two-day execution latency. Honest limitations are discussed, including the non-significance of the trailing-stop contribution under permutation and the look-ahead risk in full-sample calibration.

detail.abstract: The Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records (2017) enabled the use and transfer of electronic and digital trade documents across borders. This Model Law influenced the enactment of the Electronic Trade Documents Act (2023) (ETDA) in the United Kingdom which is a pioneer in this regard. In implementing the Model Law, however, Parliament used permissive wording and allowed significant discretion regarding the assessment of the reliability, integrity and recognition of electronic trade documents. This has caused significant legal uncertainty which parties can deploy when they try to avoid foreign obligations. The defence of public policy is one way by which parties can try to frustrate the efficient circulation of electronic trade documents. Although English courts apply public policy within a narrow scope, they usually need to hear such applications and determine them which can be burdensome. This article critically examines relevant provisions of the ETDA vis-à-vis the evolving technology and the lack of guidance apart from factors that the courts may consider. Detailed analysis is then provided to show how courts can circumvent or mitigate the legal uncertainty by using public policy in a positive manner. This involves a consideration of relevant policies underpinning electronic trade documents. A major argument is that there is ample scope to apply English public policy in a way that promotes the circulation of ETDs. This argument is then complemented by an examination of how mandatory rules can serve as a basis to further determine what could be saved from the foreign law considering the vague criteria in section 2(5) of the ETDA.

detail.abstract:
The loyalty industry stands at a technological and strategic inflection point. For three decades, loyalty programs have evolved from simple points-accumulation systems to sophisticated programmatic rule engines to trained machine learning models—each generation more capable than the last, yet each sharing a fundamental limitation: the system does what a human designed it to do. This paper introduces Self-Learning Loyalty as a formal framework for the next generation of loyalty intelligence: AI-enabled systems that observe customer behavioral events in real time, continuously update their predictive models without human retraining cycles, and generate measurable incremental outcomes at the individual level.

The paper defines the architectural components of a Self-Learning Loyalty system—including the event streaming backbone, unified identity graph, portfolio-level decisioning engine, activation and orchestration layer, and closed-loop measurement system—and distinguishes this architecture from prior generations of loyalty technology. It then identifies the most consequential unsolved problem in deploying self-learning systems at enterprise scale: the cold start problem, wherein a system with no prior behavioral history lacks a principled basis for its initial predictions. A solution is proposed in the form of expert-initialized model weights derived from structured loyalty domain expertise, alongside a new practitioner role required to govern this transition: the Data Boundary Architect. This role represents a reinvention of the loyalty strategist's function, from program designer to governance architect and from tier economist to signal boundary specialist. Finally, the paper argues that Self-Learning Loyalty changes not only program execution but also the financial use of loyalty data, because causal incrementality estimates can improve revenue forecasting, funded-offer pricing, and forward-looking business planning.

detail.abstract:
Justice Decision Observability™ (JDO™) introduces a governance discipline focused on improving visibility into human decision-making within AI-supported and operational justice environments.

Existing approaches often emphasize system outputs, compliance, and post-incident analysis. While valuable, these approaches may provide limited visibility into how decisions are interpreted, formed, and executed in real-world operational conditions.

This manifesto identifies a critical layer between signal and outcome—where human interpretation and authority shape results. By defining this space, JDO™ provides a structured lens for examining decision-making behavior and introduces a foundation for observing and reconstructing decision pathways.

This document establishes the field, defines its conceptual scope, and introduces the need for structured approaches to understanding decision environments.

title: Effective Advertising, Demand Creation, and Equilibrium Price: A Dynamic Analysis Under Monopolistic Competition

detail.title: Effective Advertising, Demand Creation, and Equilibrium Price: A Dynamic Analysis Under Monopolistic Competition
detail.abstract: Conventional economic theories adopt a static framework to analyze the relationship between advertising and market equilibrium, treating advertising expenditure as a direct addition to firms' costs and thus concluding that advertising raises product prices. Based on the market structure of monopolistic competition, this paper systematically revises this traditional view. It argues that the core value of effective advertising lies not in the redistribution of existing demand, but in awakening, activating, and creating latent demand, which shifts the overall market demand curve outward. As effective advertising expands the scale of demand, firms achieve significant economies of scale in production, supply chains, marketing, and research and development. Such scale effects push marginal cost and marginal revenue curves downward structurally, moving the profit-maximizing equilibrium toward higher output and lower prices and forming a new equilibrium marked by falling rather than rising prices. Through logical deduction, theoretical critique, and realistic mechanism verification, this paper shows that traditional conclusions rely on static assumptions and partial analysis and ignore the critical chain from demand expansion to cost reduction. The dynamic framework of demand creation, cost reduction, and price decline developed here better explains the widespread low-price competition in advertising-intensive industries and provides a more powerful analytical tool for understanding the economic function of advertising, long-run equilibrium in monopolistic competition, and changes in consumer welfare.

detail.abstract:
This paper documents the arrival of South American and Latin American fashion brands in Argentina during the 2024–2026 cycle, in parallel with the international opening described in Volume I of the DNIMLAB Market Series. While Volume I analyzed the entry of European, North American and Asian brands (Bestseller, H&M, Mango, Victoria's Secret, Longchamp, Adolfo Domínguez, On, Salomon, Dr. Martens, among others), this second volume addresses a parallel phenomenon that has received less coverage in local business press and is frequently omitted from official accounts of the cycle.

The fieldwork confirms three consolidated cases with operational physical presence as of April 2026: Indian, the Uruguayan chain owned by Grupo Chic Parisien, with nine stores open at year-end 2025 and a plan for fifty points of sale by 2027; Farm Rio, the Brazilian brand of the Azzas 2154 group operated in Argentina by Grupo Markova since December 2025; and Lili Pink, the Colombian firm of Grupo Moda para Todos, present since June 2025 with two operating stores and a plan for ten by the end of 2026. A hybrid model of growing relevance is added to these cases: Tricot, the Chilean chain with over seventy years of trajectory that entered the Argentine market in October 2025 exclusively through the digital channel; and a fourth block of arrivals announced for 2026 (Osklen, Penalty and Track & Field, all managed by Grupo Dass) that had not yet materialized physical stores at the editorial close of this paper.

The central argument is that the regional axis is not an accessory chapter of the opening cycle but a structural dimension. The paper documents three distinctive patterns: the leveraging of the Argentine tourism corridor toward Punta del Este and Florianópolis as a platform for prior brand awareness; lower logistical friction compared to European or Asian arrivals; and the emergence of regional operators with vertically integrated value chains competing with Shein and Temu in the low-cost segment. The analysis is grounded in triangulation of 2024–2026 business press, official communication from operators, and the DNIMLAB Codici Blu archive.

detail.abstract: Despite two decades of platform expansion, course abandonment rates in self-directed digital skill learning remain structurally high. This study investigates two related questions: which factors are independently associated with course abandonment among online digital skill learners, and whether peer-to-peer (P2P) engagement frequency is associated with higher digital skill self-efficacy? A quantitative, cross-sectional survey was administered to 147 respondents (79.6% aged 18-24; 81.0% undergraduate students) at a University of Delhi institution. Seven dropout predictors were tested in a binary logistic regression; P2P engagement was examined through a binary group comparison, a frequency-based sensitivity analysis, and a Spearman dose-response correlation with confidence. The regression model was collectively significant (χ²(7) = 20.79, p = .004; Nagelkerke R 2 = .203; accuracy = 79.6%). The primary modifiable predictors were timely feedback (Q20 itemlevel OR = 0.548, 95% bootstrap CI [0.278, 0.784]) and cost barrier (OR = 2.772, 95% CI [1.068, 14.73]). These findings replace the originally reported Feedback Quality composite (Cronbach's α =-1.408), which is rendered psychometrically invalid by the negative inter-item correlation of its constituent items; item-level re-analysis confirms Q20 ("the course provided timely and useful feedback") as the primary signal, while Q21_R contributes no independent significant effect. A principal component analysis of the seven items underlying the intercorrelated structural barrier predictors (Unresolved Doubts, Time Constraints, Social Isolation) confirms that a single latent factor accounts for 59.0% of their shared variance. The binary P2P group comparison was directionally supported but statistically inconclusive (t(145) = 1.516, p = .132; 46% power). A frequency-threshold sensitivity analysis (Low ≤ 2.5 vs. High ≥ 3.5) yielded a significant and medium-large difference (t(112) = 3.068, p = .003; d = 0.635). The dose-response correlation confirmed a significant positive association between P2P engagement frequency and confidence (Spearman ρ = .243, p = .003). All findings are reported as associations; the cross-sectional design does not support causal inference.

title: Regulating the Algorithmic Society: Governance Challenges in the Age of AI and Big Data

detail.title: Regulating the Algorithmic Society: Governance Challenges in the Age of AI and Big Data
detail.abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) and big data technologies is transforming contemporary societies into algorithmically mediated environments. These developments generate unprecedented opportunities for innovation, economic growth, and public sector efficiency, while simultaneously raising complex governance challenges related to accountability, transparency, privacy, and fairness. This article examines the emerging regulatory landscape of the algorithmic society, with particular emphasis on the European Union's approach to balancing innovation with fundamental rights protection. It explores key governance issues including algorithmic bias, data asymmetries, cross-border data flows, and institutional capacity gaps. By analyzing recent policy frameworks and regulatory instruments, the paper argues for a multi-level, adaptive governance model that integrates legal, technical, and ethical dimensions. The article concludes with recommendations for strengthening regulatory coherence, enhancing public trust, and ensuring responsible AI deployment in an increasingly datadriven world.

title: The Impact of AI on Branding and Brand Equity Management

detail.title: The Impact of AI on Branding and Brand Equity Management
detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed the field of branding and brand equity management by enabling organizations to adopt more data-driven, personalized, and efficient strategies. This study explores how AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and predictive analytics influence brand building and customer engagement. AI enhances brand awareness through targeted advertising, strengthens brand associations by analyzing consumer sentiment, and improves perceived quality through consistent service delivery. Additionally, AI-driven personalization and loyalty programs play a crucial role in increasing customer retention and brand loyalty.

The paper also highlights the advantages of AI, including improved decision-making, operational efficiency, and enhanced customer experience, while addressing key challenges such as data privacy concerns, ethical issues, and the potential loss of human touch. Through real-world examples of companies like Amazon, Netflix, and Nike, the study demonstrates the practical application of AI in modern branding. The findings suggest that while AI is a powerful tool for strengthening brand equity, a balanced approach combining technology with human creativity and ethical considerations is essential for long-term success.

detail.abstract:
Physical retail lives inside a contradiction. It is saturated with data and yet remains surprisingly poor at understanding meaning while choice is still forming. Retailers can often tell what was stocked, what was visible, what was touched, what was promoted, what was scanned, and what was ultimately purchased. They can measure traffic, dwell, conversion, price realization, shelf availability, assortment movement, and operational compliance with increasing sophistication. But between exposure and outcome there still exists a decisive interval that is only weakly formalized by conventional systems: the moment in which the shopper compares, doubts, rejects, reframes, seeks reassurance, translates sensation into language, and begins to assign meaning to what stands before them. This book begins with the conviction that this interval is not marginal. It is one of the most commercially consequential and conceptually neglected zones in physical retail.

For many years, the dominant architecture of retail knowledge has been built around what is easiest to count. Inventory systems show whether a product is present. Planogram and compliance tools show whether it is placed correctly. Traffic and video systems show movement, stopping, and flow. Transaction records show what was sold. Reviews and surveys capture what some consumers say after the fact. These layers are useful and often indispensable. Yet they do not fully explain what meaning existed at the shelf while the decision was still alive. A product may be noticed but rejected for a reason that no dashboard captures. A shopper may pause not out of attraction but uncertainty. Strong footfall may coexist with semantic confusion. Weak conversion may conceal not lack of demand but a failure of positioning, language, reassurance, contextual fit, or social relevance. When interpretation depends only on lagging outcomes, firms often mistake aftermath for understanding.

That distinction matters. Outcome is not explanation. Purchase is not the same thing as interpretive resolution. An item can appear successful because it sold, yet still be misunderstood, mispositioned, or chosen for reasons very different from the ones the brand imagines. An item can appear weak because it underperformed, while the actual problem lies not in the product but in framing, adjacency, scent language, price anchoring, pack communication, or unspoken category anxiety. What is counted at the register is often the final visible residue of a much richer process that has already disappeared by the time it becomes measurable. In that sense, physical retail is frequently data-rich but meaning-poor at the point of consideration. Its strongest instruments tend to illuminate what happened after the decisive interval has already passed.

This study examines the retailer perception and acceptance of dairy-based products offered by Britannia in the Delhi NCR region. The research is based on primary data collected from 520 retailers using a structured questionnaire. The findings reveal that while Britannia enjoys strong brand recognition, especially in biscuits, its dairy products still face tough competition from established brands like Amul.

The research concludes that improving distribution efficiency, increasing promotional strategies, and strengthening retailer relationships can significantly enhance market penetration and sales of Britannia dairy products.

title: The Effect of AI on Marketing Employment: Evidence from 110m+ Online Employment Records

detail.title: The Effect of AI on Marketing Employment: Evidence from 110m+ Online Employment Records
detail.abstract: Marketing is widely considered one of the job functions most exposed to generative AI, but large-scale evidence on marketing-specific employment effects remains limited. We study how the public release of ChatGPT in November 2022 affected marketing employment using a panel of over 110 million employment records from Revelio Labs covering 164,780 firms. Comparing marketing to non-marketing employees within the same firm in a difference-in-differences design, we find that the post-ChatGPT change in average marketing headcount is 0.92% lower than the corresponding change for non-marketing headcount. We demonstrate that this relative decline is strongest among both junior and senior employees, while mid-level marketing employees are least affected relative to same-seniority non-marketing peers; and that within fields, the contraction is concentrated in non-digital marketing and customer service employees in particular, while sales employment has enjoyed a modest relative increase. Lastly, we show in triple-differences analyses that the relative decline in marketing headcount is significantly larger in firms and industries with higher pre-period AI exposure.

title: Marketing Education in Africa: A Pedagogical Review of Historical Development and Decolonial Transformation

detail.title: Marketing Education in Africa: A Pedagogical Review of Historical Development and Decolonial Transformation
detail.abstract: This paper examines the historical development of marketing in Africa through a pedagogical lens, tracing its evolution from precolonial trade networks to contemporary digital ecosystems. It explores how indigenous systems of exchange, colonial legacies, liberalization policies, and globalization have shaped marketing thought and practice across the continent. The study identifies three broad pedagogical phases: imitation, adaptation, and decolonial transformation, each reflecting shifts in Africa's socioeconomic and epistemological contexts. Drawing from historical, cultural, and theoretical perspectives, the paper critiques the dominance of Western marketing paradigms and argues for a decolonial, context-sensitive pedagogy rooted in African epistemologies, ethics, and lived realities. The analysis highlights Africa's unique contributions to relational marketing, social entrepreneurship, and digital innovation. Finally, it proposes pedagogical strategies emphasizing experiential learning, linguistic diversity, and Ubuntu ethics to align marketing education with Africa's developmental aspirations. The paper concludes that re-centering African knowledge systems is essential for building an inclusive, globally relevant, and socially responsible marketing discipline.
